notes.summary: Proved a draft of M1–M3 and actual all-point resolved-nef fiber constancy on BJ Definition 4.1 varying-class decreasing nets, using one graph-dominating semistable model and fixed-support canonical curvature. Scalar descent is usc; genuine target membership is still a separate gate.
notes.detailedSummary: Numerical triviality survives algebraically closed extension by spreading one proper curve and specializing its line-bundle degree via constant Euler characteristics. This supplies continuous finite degree functionals on N1. For each fixed auxiliary smooth proper fiber curve over complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued K, BE5.13 gives one graph model; BE4.20 is used only in its algebraically closed auxiliary case, and Temkin stable modification gives actual domination. Constant composite factors scheme-theoretically through the extended section. All canonical varying Li references pull from that model and have fixed finite type-II curvature support with nonnegative coefficients tending to zero. Exact ddc(phi_i)=mu_i-nu_i and correctly signed fixed Green corrections give harmonic comparison by decreasing original-net boundary compactness, without making the corrected functions decrease. Floors stay in the same nef class. Geometrically connected fibers, separate residue-field extensions to one closed reference point, and finite curve-morphism chains identify every analytic value. Proper closed superlevels give usc scalar descent. These combined primary applications remain unverified.

Auxiliary curve fields are separately chosen complete, algebraically closed and NONTRIVIALLY valued. All arguments are unverified proof drafts. ## 2. A numerical specialization lemma

We first prove the numerical fact needed for the **varying-class** net. Let $Z$ be projective over algebraically closed $k$, let $\Omega/k$ be an algebraically closed extension, and let $D$ be a line bundle numerically trivial on $Z$. Then $D_\Omega$ is numerically trivial on $Z_\Omega$. More generally, for a fixed proper integral curve $T/\Omega$ and morphism $a:T\to Z_\Omega$, the rule
$$[D]\longmapsto \deg_\Omega a^*D_\Omega                                      \tag{2.1}$$
factors through a finite continuous linear functional on $N^1(Z)_\mathbb R$.

Here is the finite-data proof. Embed $T$ in a projective space and write its equations, the finite morphism charts of $a$, and the equations identifying its generic fiber over a finitely generated integral $k$-subalgebra $A\subset\Omega$. Clearing the finite denominators gives a projective finitely presented family $\mathcal T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ and a morphism $\mathcal T\to Z_A$, with $\mathcal T_\Omega=T$. Shrink this integral base once so that $\mathcal T$ is flat. This is generic flatness for a finite type family over a noetherian integral ring; it applies because the generic fiber is a curve. Shrink further to make the geometric fibers integral curves. The generic fiber is geometrically integral: its base extension to the algebraically closed $\Omega$ is integral, so geometric integrality descends. Openness of geometric integrality for a flat finitely presented family then applies. Only finitely many equations and this one curve are being spread out.

For each fixed $D$, the pullback $\mathcal D$ is invertible and is flat over $A$, since $\mathcal T$ is flat. Both $\mathcal D$ and $\mathcal O_\mathcal T$ are finitely presented. Proper flat finite-presentation Euler-characteristic constancy (Stacks 0B9T) gives constant $\chi(\mathcal D_t)$ and $\chi(\mathcal O_{\mathcal T_t})$ on the connected remaining base, and these characteristics commute with field extension. On an integral proper curve the degree of an invertible sheaf is their difference. Choose a closed $k$-point $t$ of the nonempty open base; its residue field is $k$ by the Nullstellensatz. The projection formula gives
$$\deg a_t^*D=\begin{cases}
e\deg(D|_{a_t(T_t)})&\text{if the image is a curve of generic degree }e,\\
0&\text{if the image is a point}.
\end{cases}$$
It is zero when $D$ is numerically trivial. The same Euler-characteristic difference computes the degree on $T$, proving the assertion. It is not necessary to descend infinitely many $D$ simultaneously: the assertion that the numerical kernel is annihilated is checked one $D$ at a time. Additivity of degree first gives a homomorphism on $\operatorname{Pic}(Z)$, then a $\mathbb Q$-linear map on $N^1(Z)_\mathbb Q$, and finally a real linear map on the finite dimensional $N^1(Z)_\mathbb R$. Every such linear map is continuous. Thus numerical convergence of classes suffices; Picard convergence is neither assumed nor needed.

The same argument proves nefness ascends under algebraically closed field extension: every new curve specializes as above, and a nonnegative degree remains nonnegative. Nefness descends by extending each old integral curve and preserving its degree. Degree is unchanged on an integral curve under field extension, since the cohomology dimensions, and hence the Euler-characteristic difference, are unchanged. These arguments also apply to proper curve morphisms, not only embedded curves. Ampleness of an actual line bundle ascends and descends by fpqc descent of relative ampleness (Stacks 0D3C); it is not deduced merely from nefness.

## 3. One graph model for every canonical reference (M1)

Fix $s\in X^{\rm an}$, put $F=\mathscr H(s)$, and choose a complete algebraically closed **nontrivially valued** extension $K/F$. Let $R=K^\circ$ and $\widetilde K$ be its algebraically closed residue field. In this section fix a smooth proper connected algebraic curve $C/K$ and a morphism $f:C\to Y_K$ with constant composite to $X_K$, equal to the $K$-point induced by $s$. A smooth proper curve over a field is projective. The maps $k\to K$ and $k\to\widetilde K$ are injective because $k$ is trivially valued; in particular both fields have characteristic zero.

Take **the actual BJ Definition 4.1** representation of a bounded $\varphi\in\operatorname{PSH}(Y,\pi^*c_1(L))$:
$$\varphi_i\in\mathcal H_{\mathbb R}^{\rm gf}(L_i),\qquad
\varphi_i\downarrow\varphi,\qquad c_1(L_i)\longrightarrow\pi^*c_1(L).       \tag{3.1}$$
This is a directed net and the $L_i\in\operatorname{Pic}(Y)_\mathbb Q$ vary. Every $\varphi_i$ is finite valued because it dominates the bounded $\varphi$. Its finite sections therefore have no common zero, so $L_i$ is semiample. This is exactly the bounded clause following Definition 4.1, not a same-bundle regularization theorem.

Let $\mathcal Y=Y\times_k R$, the constant projective model. BE Proposition 5.13 gives the schematic flat graph closure $\mathcal G$ of $f$ in the product of **one** projective curve model and $\mathcal Y$. It is projective and flat over $R$, dominates that curve model, and carries a morphism $\mathcal G\to\mathcal Y$. Models over a valuation ring are finitely presented by BE Lemma 4.5. Take relative integral closure in the prescribed generic fiber $C$. BE Theorem 4.20 is applicable here because $K$ is algebraically closed and nontrivially valued: the closure is finite and its special fiber is reduced. Its assertion is not used over an arbitrary nondiscrete valuation ring; BE Remark 4.21 explicitly forbids that generalization.

A semistable model must dominate this chosen graph; existence of an unrelated semistable model would not suffice. Apply Temkin's stable-modification theorem (0707.3953v3, Theorems 1.1 and 1.5; Proposition 4.5.1 and its gluing proof) to the resulting projective $R$-curve with empty marking. Check pure relative dimension one as follows. The graph and its relative integral closure are integral and have generic fiber the proper connected smooth $C$, whose global functions are $K$. Stacks 0AY8 applies over the normal integral target $\operatorname{Spec}R$: the map is proper, its source reduced, its generic point dominates, and its generic global functions are $K$. Its special fiber is therefore connected. For an actual relatively very ample bundle, Euler-characteristic constancy (0B9T) applied to each twist makes its special Hilbert polynomial equal to the generic linear Hilbert polynomial. Thus its special fiber has maximum dimension one. A zero-dimensional irreducible component of a reduced finite-type scheme over an algebraically closed field is an isolated open-and-closed point: it cannot lie in another component, and there are only finitely many components. Connectedness excludes such a component. All special components consequently have dimension one, as do the generic components. The graph is flat and finitely presented, so it is precisely a multipointed $R$-curve with empty marking in Temkin's definitions in Section 1.1. The generic fiber is smooth and hence semistable.

For clarity the alteration in Theorem 1.5 does not change our chosen field. Over $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, choose a component of its generically etale proper alteration $S'\to S$. Its generic field is finite separable over $K$, hence is $K$ since $K$ is algebraically closed. The resulting $K$-point extends to a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\to S'$ by properness. Pulling the stable modification back along this section gives a semistable $R$-curve $\mathcal C$ with a proper generic-fiber identity map $\mathcal C\to\mathcal G$. It is projective by Temkin 1.1. This is an actual domination of the chosen graph. Completion at any $0<|a|<1$ gives an admissible proper formal model. If a strictly semistable model is desired, subdivide the finite skeleton by adding type II vertices to remove loops; BPR 3.13, 3.14 and 4.11 identify these refinements with dominating formal models. The original morphism to $\mathcal Y$ is retained. We use no purported cofinality assertion about an arbitrary initial semistable model.

All canonical references of the $L_i$ are now represented on the **same** model:
$$\mathcal M_i=\mathcal f^*(L_i\otimes_kR).                              \tag{3.2}$$
The reference on $L_i$ is the canonical trivial metric over $k$, pulled to $K$. BE 5.10 and 5.13 identify this pullback exactly with the metric of (3.2). The equality concerns the original bundles and their trivializations. Since $L_i$ is semiample, the canonical reference is also its pure FS metric: a generating system on a divisible power has maximum norm one in the center frame at each point. This gives an independent check of both its positivity and its precise reference. No infinite list of bundles is algebraized on the curve; each already comes from the one fixed constant $\mathcal Y$.

Finally the composite $\mathcal C\to X_R$ factors through the unique extended section $\bar s:\operatorname{Spec}R\to X_R$. The generic constant point extends uniquely by projectivity/separatedness. The composite and $\bar s\circ(\mathcal C\to\operatorname{Spec}R)$ coincide on the generic fiber. The equalizer is closed by separatedness, and flatness makes that generic fiber schematically dense: on each affine chart localization into its generic-fiber ring is injective because the ring is $R$-torsion free. Therefore the equalizer is the whole model as a scheme. This is stronger than topological agreement on a dense set.

## 4. Fixed background curvature and vanishing coefficients (M2--M3)

Let $E$ run over the finitely many irreducible components of the reduced special fiber of $\mathcal C$, and $\zeta_E$ be their type II Shilov points. The set $\Sigma=\{\zeta_E\}$ is fixed independently of $i$. Let $h_{0,i}^C$ denote the actual pulled canonical metric on $f^*L_i$. Its raw curvature is
$$\nu_i=c_1(f^*L_i,h_{0,i}^C)=\sum_E a_{i,E}\delta_{\zeta_E},\qquad
a_{i,E}=\deg_{\widetilde K}(\mathcal M_i|_E)\ge0.                       \tag{4.1}$$
This is BE Example 8.11, with its continuous signed-metric extension in 8.10 and the model compatibility of 8.18--8.21; on a curve it agrees with the CLD curvature current. The degree of a rational bundle is divided by its cleared tensor denominator. This division must not be omitted.

Here are the multiplicity and residue conventions in (4.1). The special fundamental cycle is $[\mathcal C_s]=\sum_E\ell_E[E]$, with $\ell_E$ the generic length. A degree over a nonalgebraically closed residue field already includes the factor $[k_E:\widetilde K]$, where $k_E$ is the finite constant field of the proper integral component, relative to the degree over $k_E$. Thus an unnormalized cycle formula would contain $\ell_E[k_E:\widetilde K]\deg_{k_E}(\mathcal M_i|_E)$. In our application $\ell_E=1$ and $k_E=\widetilde K$: reduced special fiber and algebraically closed residue field have actually been established. We do not use $\operatorname{ord}_E(t)$ over the nondiscrete $R$, which has no distinguished uniformizer. In discretely valued test-configuration formulas the usual multiplicity $b_E=\operatorname{ord}_E(t)$ is instead retained. Nilpotents are never erased when computing a cycle or measure.

The positivity of each coefficient follows also directly: $\mathcal M_i|_E$ is the pullback of the semiample $(L_i)_{\widetilde K}$ through $E\to Y_{\widetilde K}$ and so has nonnegative degree. Denote this fixed degree functional on $N^1(Y)$ by $\lambda_E$. Section 2 proves it is well defined and continuous even though $E$ and its morphism need not descend to $k$. The model factorization in Section 3 says $\pi\circ f_E$ is constant. Hence
$$\lambda_E(\pi^*c_1(L))=0,\qquad
a_{i,E}=\lambda_E(c_1(L_i))\longrightarrow0.                            \tag{4.2}$$
There are finitely many $E$, so $\nu_i(C^{\rm an})=\sum_Ea_{i,E}\to0$. This is numerical convergence, not convergence of line bundles. It also agrees with the generic-fiber degree by flat Euler-characteristic constancy.

Let $h_i^C=h_{0,i}^C+\varphi_i^C$ be the FS metric obtained by restricting the actual $i$th sections and keeping their finite real weights. Write $\mu_i=c_1(f^*L_i,h_i^C)$. It is positive by continuous FS positivity (BE 7.14, 8.3--8.5). Subtracting the two metrics on **the same** $f^*L_i$ gives the exact distribution identity
$$dd^c\varphi_i^C=\mu_i-\nu_i.                                        \tag{4.3}$$
Its verification is local: in any common frame subtract $h_{0,i}^C$ from $h_i^C$, so transition logarithms cancel. The continuous raw curve measures represent the corresponding CLD currents; for a semistable model difference this is Wanner 3.27--3.28, and continuous dpsh extension follows by the uniform regularizations in BE. The backgrounds do not silently switch to a fixed ample metric. Both $\mu_i$ and $\nu_i$ have the same raw degree, but only $\nu_i$ needs the fixed support.

## 5. Correct Green sign and passage of the decreasing net

Take a connected strict affinoid domain $V$ in $C^{\rm an}$ with nonempty boundary disjoint from $\Sigma$. For each $\zeta\in\Sigma\cap V$, Thuillier 3.3.7(ii) provides a continuous lisse Green function $g_\zeta^V$, zero on $\partial V$, with
$$dd^cg_\zeta^V=-\delta_\zeta\quad\text{on }V\setminus\partial V.
$$
The boundary measure is not discarded globally. Put
$$p_i=-\sum_{\zeta\in\Sigma\cap V}a_{i,\zeta}g_\zeta^V.                 \tag{5.1}$$
Then $dd^cp_i=\nu_i$ on the interior and
$$\|p_i\|_V\le\sum_{\zeta\in\Sigma\cap V}a_{i,\zeta}\|g_\zeta^V\|_V
\longrightarrow0.                                                    \tag{5.2}$$
This proves uniform zero correction. It uses **fixed**, bounded Green functions and a finite support. A small mass with moving poles would not prove (5.2).

The functions $u_i=\varphi_i^C+p_i$ are continuous and have positive CLD current on the interior by (4.3). All hypotheses of Wanner Theorem 4.7 hold: $K$ is algebraically closed, complete and nontrivially valued; $C$ is a smooth proper algebraic curve; the tested set is an ordinary open; and the functions are finite continuous there. They are therefore Thuillier subharmonic. They need not decrease.

We spell out the net argument. Let $q$ be continuous and harmonic on $V$ and suppose $\varphi^C\le q$ on $\partial V$. For $\epsilon>0$, the closed boundary sets
$$\{x\in\partial V:\varphi_i^C(x)\ge q(x)+\epsilon\}$$
decrease and have empty intersection. Compactness and directedness give one index after which all are empty. At the same time (5.2) gives $|p_i|<\epsilon$. Subharmonic comparison yields $u_i\le q+2\epsilon$ on $V$, and hence $\varphi_i^C\le q+3\epsilon$. Take the decreasing original limit and then $\epsilon\downarrow0$. This is finite-intersection boundary comparison, not Dini for a possibly discontinuous limit and not monotone convergence of the corrected functions.

There is a simple way to cover also test domains whose boundaries meet $\Sigma$, without asserting an unproved restricted-basis criterion. For any proper strict affinoid $W$, choose a type II point $\eta$ outside $W$. Thuillier 3.3.7(i) gives bounded global lisse functions $g_{\zeta,\eta}$ with $dd^cg_{\zeta,\eta}=\delta_\eta-\delta_\zeta$. Use $p_i'=-\sum_{\zeta\in\Sigma}a_{i,\zeta}g_{\zeta,\eta}$. Its norm goes to zero on the proper curve and its curvature is $\nu_i-(\sum a_{i,\zeta})\delta_\eta$. Thus $\varphi_i^C+p_i'$ is subharmonic on a neighborhood of $W$. The identical boundary argument proves harmonic comparison on every such $W$. These are exactly Thuillier's comparison tests. The bounded usc function $\varphi^C$ is consequently subharmonic on the whole curve and is not identically $-\infty$.

On a proper connected curve it attains a finite maximum. Thuillier 3.1.11 gives local constancy at any local maximum. The maximum set is closed by usc and open by that principle, hence is the whole connected curve. Therefore
$$\varphi\circ f^{\rm an}\quad\text{is constant on }C^{\rm an}.          \tag{5.3}$$
This establishes the curve-constancy consequence of M1--M3 on the actual Definition 4.1 net. No affine regularization over $K$, no same-class FS net, and no Picard convergence has been used.

## 6. All analytic fiber points have the same value

First justify geometric connectedness. The finite normalization $\nu:X^\nu\to X$ is a universal homeomorphism by Stacks 0GIQ, since $X$ is irreducible geometrically unibranch. The normal-target map $\rho:Y\to X^\nu$ satisfies all six assumptions of Stacks 0AY8: it is proper; its target is integral and normal; its source is reduced; its single generic point maps to the target generic point; and its generic fiber has $H^0=k(X)$. The normal-target Stein factor is therefore the target, and every fiber is geometrically connected.

For any field point $\operatorname{Spec}F\to X$ the normalization fiber is finite radicial. In characteristic zero its unique residue field is $F$, so its reduction is $\operatorname{Spec}F$, though it may have nilpotents. Reducing after an algebraic closure gives the same underlying topological fiber of $\rho$. Hence every geometric fiber of $\pi$ is connected. This reduction is used only for connectivity and curves. It is never used to replace a fundamental cycle in a measure identity.

Fix $s\in X^{\rm an}$ and **one** closed point $z$ of the nonempty projective $F$-fiber $Y_s$, where $F=\mathscr H(s)$. Its residue field $F_z/F$ is finite. The complete norm of $F$ extends uniquely to $F_z$, giving a fixed analytic point $z^{\rm an}$ over $s$. Now let $y$ be any analytic point over $s$. Embed $\mathscr H(y)$ isometrically into a complete algebraically closed nontrivially valued field $K_y$. If its norm was trivial, first adjoin a Gauss variable with radius $0<r<1$ and complete an algebraic closure. Choose an $F$-embedding of $F_z$ into $K_y$; the unique norm-extension property makes this embedding isometric. This is done separately for each $y$, with the same original $z$. It provides $K_y$-rational lifts of $y$ and $z^{\rm an}$ to the geometric fiber. We do not descend a family of analytic points to a common field.

In a connected reduced projective fiber over algebraically closed $K_y$, the finite graph of irreducible components joined by nonempty intersections is connected. Choose closed points in each intersection along a path between components containing the two lifts. Within one component $T$, use a projective resolution $\widetilde T\to T$ in characteristic zero, and choose points above the two tested points. Here is an explicit smooth curve-morphism connection. If $\dim T=0$ there is no step; if it is one the smooth proper resolution itself suffices. If its dimension is $d\ge2$, blow up the two distinct chosen points on the smooth projective $\widetilde T$. Choose a very ample bundle on this smooth connected blowup. Iteratively take $d-1$ general hyperplane sections. Stacks 0FD6 gives smoothness (generated bundle and an immersion); 0FD9 gives connectedness at each stage, since the intermediate smooth scheme has dimension at least two and hence depth at closed points at least two. Smooth connected schemes here are irreducible. Impose also proper intersection with each exceptional divisor, an open condition on the finite tuple of hyperplanes. The final smooth connected proper curve meets each exceptional divisor: its intersection number with it is the positive top self-intersection of the ample restriction on that $\mathbb P^{d-1}$. Its composite map to $T$ therefore passes through both original points. This is a morphism, not an assumption that an embedded curve in the singular component is smooth.

The resulting finite chain consists of smooth proper connected curve morphisms into $Y_{K_y}$ whose composites to $X_{K_y}$ are constant. Section 5 applies to each. It follows that $\varphi(y)=\varphi(z^{\rm an})$ for every $y$ in the fiber, for bounded genuine $\varphi$.

For arbitrary genuine $\varphi\in\operatorname{PSH}(Y,\pi^*L)$, the floors $\max(\varphi,-m)$ remain genuine in the **same nef class**: constants are psh in a nef class by BJ 4.3, and finite maxima are stable by BJ 4.7. Apply the bounded result and let $m\to\infty$. This proves actual equality of values, including $-\infty$, on each analytic fiber. Density plus usc is not used to determine those values.

Define $\psi(s)$ to be this common value. It is usc: for every real $a$, the superlevel $\{\psi\ge a\}$ is the image under the proper analytic map $\pi^{\rm an}$ of the closed superlevel $\{\varphi\ge a\}$. Proper maps between these compact Hausdorff spaces are closed. It is generically finite since the generic trivial valuation upstairs maps to the generic trivial valuation downstairs. We have proved scalar descent and usc; genuine original-class membership is the next gate, not a consequence of these topological assertions.

## 7. Exact original reference requirement and C1

For a frame $e$ of the original $L$ on $U\subset X$, write $h_{0,e}=-\log\|e\|_0$ for its canonical reference weight. The descended metric must have the weight
$$b_e=\psi+h_{0,e},\qquad
b_e=b_{e'}-\log|e/e'|,\qquad
\pi^*b_e=\varphi+\pi^*h_{0,e}.                                        \tag{7.1}$$
The pulled reference is exactly the canonical reference on $\pi^*L$, by pullback of the constant model; it is not one of the varying $L_i$ unless they actually equal $\pi^*L$. Formula (7.1) proves cocycle compatibility, but Definition 4.1 alone supplies no convergence of the different $h_{0,i}$ to $\pi^*h_{0,e}$. We now prove the actual local contact application by changing the approximating classes in a controlled, justified way.

**Original-reference contact lemma.** Fix a very ample actual bundle $A$ on $Y$, with its canonical metric. Write $\theta=\pi^*c_1(L)$. The function $\varphi$ is already genuine on $Y$, so actual BJ 12.18(ii) applies: it gives a decreasing sequence $a_j\in H(M_j)$, with $M_j$ ample rational bundles, $c_1(M_j)\to\theta$, and $a_j\downarrow\varphi$. This source theorem has varying bundles and does not assume EP on $X$. Its countable regularization proof uses the already constructed genuine energy theory; it is not a first-membership theorem and is not regularization on the nef $\pi^*L$.

Put $\delta_r=2^{-r}$. By numerical convergence and openness of the ample cone, choose an increasing subsequence $j(r)$ so that
$$\delta_r c_1(A)-(c_1(M_{j(r)})-\theta)\text{ is ample}.                 \tag{7.2}$$
Indeed, the open neighborhood $\delta_r c_1(A)-\operatorname{Amp}(Y)$ of zero contains the numerical difference eventually. Constants are psh in this nef difference, and BJ 4.7 therefore gives $a_{j(r)}\in\operatorname{PSH}(Y,B_r)$ for the **actual** ample rational bundle
$$B_r=\pi^*L+\delta_r A.$$
This class change is proved by adding the constant zero; there is no identification of $M_{j(r)}$ with $B_r$ or claim about their Picard distance. Each $a_{j(r)}$ is finite continuous. BJ 4.16 and Example 3.9 now give $q_r\in H(B_r)$ with rational weights and $\|q_r-a_{j(r)}\|_\infty<\epsilon_r=4^{-r}$. These are approximations in the same actual $B_r$ at the fixed $r$, whose existence follows from continuous genuine membership in that ample class. The bundles $B_r$ vary.

Set $c_r=2\sum_{l\ge r}\epsilon_l=\frac83\,4^{-r}$. The difference
$$q_r+c_r-q_{r+1}-c_{r+1}\ge2\epsilon_r-\epsilon_r-\epsilon_{r+1}>0$$
shows $q_r+c_r\downarrow\varphi$. The limit is unchanged because the uniform approximation errors and shifts go to zero. All shifts are rational.

Cover $Y$ by the finite section frames $s$ of a generating system of the very ample $A$. On $D(s)$ its canonical reference weight is $h_{A,s}=\max_l\log|s_l/s|\ge0$, with the branch $s/s=1$. On $\pi^{-1}U\cap D(s)$, tensor multiplicativity of the actual canonical metrics gives the reference of $B_r$ exactly as $\pi^*h_{0,e}+\delta_r h_{A,s}$. Consequently the weights
$$w_r=q_r+c_r+\pi^*h_{0,e}+\delta_r h_{A,s}                            \tag{7.3}$$
decrease to $\varphi+\pi^*h_{0,e}$ on this one common ordinary open: both variable terms decrease and $h_{A,s}\ge0$ is finite there. Each $w_r$ is precisely the local weight of its rational FS metric on $B_r$, plus the rational constant $c_r$. Clear its tensor denominator; in the frame $e\otimes s^{\delta_r}$ it is a finite maximum of rational multiples of logarithms of regular section coefficients, plus rational constants, in the **original ring of this witness chart**. The generating sections have no common zero. At any tested point choose a maximizing nonzero branch. Its rational affine expression lies below the maximum and equals it with the same constant. Branches vanishing there are inactive and can be removed on a smaller point neighborhood; a sufficiently low rational floor is inactive on a compact smaller neighborhood. Thus the supplied exact rational contact condition holds, including its finite-floor convention. The functions for the entire sequence are defined on the common chart; unit reductions may be made separately when testing each continuous approximant. For any finite tuple the intersections give one common ordinary neighborhood.

This proves that every original-frame resolved weight is locally a decreasing rational contact limit on the **one** witness $Y$. It proves the required R-original application, including unbounded $\varphi$, since BJ 12.18(ii) gives finite continuous approximants even then. Alternatively bounded floors stay in the same nef class by Section 6. No field extension or affine regularization over a completed residue field occurs in this construction. The M1--M3 proof still used the actual Definition 4.1 net; this separate contact lemma does not replace it by a fictitious same-bundle net.

The sole remaining analytic hypothesis is now stated in weak-to-genuine form:

**C1-original (conditional).** Over every countable algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, an original geometrically unibranch projective $X$ with actual ample rational $L$ has the following global membership theorem. If a generically finite usc scalar $\psi$ has original weights $\psi+h_{0,e}$ with the actual $L$ cocycle, and their pullbacks on one proper birational smooth witness are locally decreasing rational contact limits in the exact task-granted sense, then $\psi\in\operatorname{PSH}(X,L)$ in BJ Definition 4.1. All required geometric compactification/domination/resolution-witness antecedents must be included in that theorem's scope. No completed-field version is required or asserted.

Sections 6 and (7.1)--(7.3) verify these admissibility and reference hypotheses for our descended scalar. If the countable theorem also formulates an upper-growth condition, it is present here: $\sup\psi=\sup\varphi<\infty$ by the generic-trivial-value formula for genuine potentials, and in the section frame of a sufficiently divisible very ample original $L$ the reference $h_{0,e}$ is a finite affine FS maximum in the original section ratios. Thus $b_e\le h_{0,e}+\sup\psi$ has the actual original upper-growth reference, with generators appended at dominated weights as in the task-granted localization construction. One may first apply C1 to the bounded scalar floors and then use genuine decreasing closure for the unbounded limit. C1 supplies the remaining global membership conclusion, not a smooth or changed-class conclusion. This hypothesis is neither proved here nor inferred from Wu's printed result or independent Runge work.

Assuming C1-original, pullback is onto. Its forward inclusion is BJ 4.7; injectivity is analytic surjectivity. The divisorial sets on $X$ and $Y$ are the identical valuations of their common function field (including the trivial valuation), not separate dense sets. Their BJ topologies are pointwise convergence on these sets; hence the bijection is a homeomorphism. Analytic surjectivity also gives $\sup_X\psi=\sup_Y\pi^*\psi$. ## 8. Finite data and arbitrary cardinality

Assume henceforth countable EP just obtained conditionally. We reconstruct the full finite-data route. A finite field of definition means a finitely generated subfield of $k$ containing the finitely many coefficients in the chosen presentations, followed by its algebraic closure inside $k$. This is countable in characteristic zero. It need not contain the real constants occurring as weights; those are kept as the same finitely many real numbers, external to the coefficient field.

For finite algebraic data, descent is literal. Projective equations, finite affine presentations, transition functions of actual line bundles, finite section systems and their equalities, flag ideals, graph maps, the $\mathbb G_m$-action and its identities, and the specified generic-fiber isomorphism all involve finitely many coefficients and identities. Enlarge the countable subfield to contain them. Generation by the descended sections is detected by the coherent cokernel, which is zero after faithfully flat extension iff it was zero. An integral/reduced projective scheme downstairs is detected in the same manner; since the field is algebraically closed and characteristic zero it is geometrically integral/reduced. Actual ample bundles and relative ample model bundles descend by fpqc ampleness. A finite birational map is descended together with a dense open on which it is an isomorphism; finiteness and that isomorphism are fpqc properties. The dense open remains nonempty since its extension is nonempty.

Descend the normalization as a **finite map with its actual source**, not as an unsupported slogan. Include its finite presentation, algebra inclusion and dense-open isomorphism. Its source is normal: normality descends through the faithfully flat field extension. Over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field it is geometrically normal (Stacks 0BXT, since the field is already perfect). The finite birational normal source is therefore the normalization and remains so after any field enlargement. Its universal-homeomorphism property also descends: after extending algebraically closed fields, a finite map's geometric fibers and residue extensions detect universal injectivity, while surjectivity is fpqc. Equivalently the finite diagonal's surjectivity can be checked after this base change. Hence the original downstairs $X_0$ is geometrically unibranch; one has not silently replaced a nonnormal generic fiber by its normalization.

For a finite model obstacle or Hdom competitor descend its **actual generic-fiber** model and bundle. Flatness over the test line is detected faithfully flat, or directly by torsion freeness over $k_0[t]$. For relative integral closure use BJ 1.13 and 1.15: it is equivalent to vertical $R_1$ and to the special fiber having no embedded associated points (vertical $S_2$). Algebraically closed characteristic-zero field extensions are regular. In local noetherian rings the flat depth formula and the corresponding dimension formula, with regular closed fibers, preserve and reflect $S_1$; regularity preserves and reflects the regular local rings at the generic points of the central fiber. Indeed all central components over an algebraically closed field are geometrically integral, so their generic points remain precisely generic central points. BJ's two vertical conditions therefore descend and ascend. This uses only rings finite type over fields, not a false noetherian assertion for $K^\circ$.

Alternatively take relative integral closure of a descended raw model **inside its prescribed original generic fiber** and apply those same two vertical conditions to see that its base extension is the prescribed relatively integrally closed model. The closure is finite because these models are finite type over a field. Absolute normalization would change a nonnormal generic fiber and is not allowed.

Central cycle data are retained. At each generic central point the local ring is a DVR, and $b_E=\operatorname{ord}_E(t)$ equals the generic length in the special fiber. Flat field extension preserves this length (tensor a composition series, whose residue-field factors remain fields at the corresponding generic point). Each component is geometrically integral; intersection degrees of its model bundles are unchanged, by flat cohomological base change for multivariate Hilbert polynomials. Consequently relative nefness is preserved and reflected using the curve-specialization lemma of Section 2 on each projective special component, and relative ampleness uses fpqc descent. The finite divisor function, finite flag-ideal formula and finite FS section maximum are the **same scalar functions after analytic base extension**: valuation evaluation and the pulled constant references commute. No algebraic field is asked to encode a real weight.

These statements suffice for rational PL obstacles and finite Hdom competitors on an actual rational ample $L$. For a finite real PL obstacle one can either retain its finite real coefficients or approximate it uniformly by rational PL obstacles; only the rational case is needed for EP. An arbitrary real numerical class is handled later and is not incorrectly packaged as one actual rational bundle.

## 9. Raw continuous MA under complete field extension

Let $k_0\subset k$ be algebraically closed trivially valued fields, and $p:X_k^{\rm an}\to X_0^{\rm an}$ the analytic projection. It is continuous and surjective. Surjectivity follows by extending the valued residue field of any analytic point to a complete valued field containing $k$; equivalently it is analytic proper base-change surjectivity. For finite continuous genuine metrics on actual ample rational bundles,
$$p_*\left[\bigwedge_{j=1}^n
 (c_1(L_{j,k})+dd^cp^*\phi_j)\right]
=\bigwedge_{j=1}^n(c_1(L_j)+dd^c\phi_j),                               \tag{9.1}$$
and the raw mass on either side is $(L_1\cdots L_n)$.

Here is the actual operator calibration. BE Proposition 8.3(iv) states complete-field invariance for smooth metrics **with the analytic fundamental cycle**, Theorem 8.4 uniquely extends under uniform convergence, and 8.5 retains positivity and raw intersection mass. Semiample continuous FS-limit metrics are psh-regularizable by 7.14. BJ 4.16 supplies uniform FS approximation for continuous genuine potentials on an actual ample rational bundle, and BJ 7.23 identifies its raw measure with this continuous theory on the general reduced projective variety. Therefore (9.1) follows by uniform approximation and pushforward against every continuous test. This argument applies on the original singular or nonnormal $X_0$, not only its normalization.

The raw model formula provides a second calibration:
$$\sum_E b_E\big((\mathcal L_1|_E)\cdots(\mathcal L_n|_E)\big)\delta_{v_E}.
$$
The cycle multiplicities and degrees are those retained in Section 8; $v_E=b_E^{-1}\operatorname{ord}_E|_{k(X)}$. For possibly nonreduced schemes, the analytic fundamental cycle is instead the sum of generic lengths times the component cycles, and finite residue degrees enter each degree. Formula (9.1) preserves those factors, as BE 8.1--8.5 explicitly records. We do not apply it to an arbitrary discontinuous metric by a formal weak-limit definition. Only continuous metrics are used in the envelope descent; the genuine unbounded products are supplied separately by BJ 7.18--7.19.

## 10. Orthogonality bounds every finite competitor

Fix a rational $f\in\operatorname{PL}(X)$ and the actual ample rational $L$. Descend these and normalization to a countable algebraically closed $k_0$ as in Section 8. Write $f=p_0^*f_0$. Countable EP gives the finite continuous genuine envelope $\phi_0=P_{L_0}(f_0)$; a constant below $\min f_0$ is a competitor, so it is not $-\infty$. Put $\phi=p_0^*\phi_0$. Base extension of the Definition 4.1 net gives actual genuine membership of this continuous metric on $L$; the numerical pullback map is linear continuous by Section 2. The envelope satisfies $\phi\le f$.

Countable EP alone gives the two tools needed here, without importing the desired inverse equation. Orthogonality follows directly from BJ 13.1 under its explicit EP premise. For a continuous obstacle, its short proof uses the genuine energy derivative: if $g=f_0-\phi_0\ge0$, then $P(\phi_0+tg)=\phi_0$ for $0\le t\le1$, so the derivative of $E\circ P$ is zero and $\int g\,\mathrm{MA}(\phi_0)=0$. Domination is genuine BJ 10.6 and needs no EP or inverse Dirac equation. Its input is a pointwise a.e. inequality for the genuine MA of one finite-energy potential.

Take any finite Hdom competitor $h$ with $h\le f$. Its finite model data may require a **new** countable algebraically closed $k_1\supset k_0$. Descend them there and write $h=p_1^*h_1$. Surjectivity of $p_1$ gives $h_1\le f_1$. The pullback $\phi_1$ of $\phi_0$ is genuine continuous. By (9.1), the nonnegative continuous integrand gives
$$\int_{X_1^{\rm an}}(f_1-\phi_1)\,\mathrm{MA}^{\rm raw}(\phi_1)
=\int_{X_0^{\rm an}}(f_0-\phi_0)\,\mathrm{MA}^{\rm raw}(\phi_0)=0.         \tag{10.1}$$
Thus $f_1=\phi_1$ a.e. for that measure, and $h_1\le\phi_1$ a.e. Domination gives $h_1\le\phi_1$ everywhere. Pull back to $k$ to get $h\le\phi$. One can also transfer (10.1) directly to $k$; the separate $k_1$ makes explicit that each finite competitor has its own field. No equality between a support and an inverse image of a support is used, and no entire family is descended.

Finally let $q\in\operatorname{PSH}(X,L)$ be **any** competitor with $q\le f$. BJ 4.15(iii), not an unsupported same-bundle regularization assertion, gives a decreasing net $h_i\in\mathrm{Hdom}(L)$ with $h_i\downarrow q$. For rational $\epsilon>0$, the closed sets $\{h_i\ge f+\epsilon\}$ on compact $X^{\rm an}$ decrease with empty intersection. Directed finite intersection gives eventual emptiness. Then $h_i-\epsilon\le f$; this remains a finite Hdom function (rational constant shift corresponds to a rational central divisor). The preceding bound applies separately to each such function, giving $h_i-\epsilon\le\phi$. Take its decreasing limit and then $\epsilon\downarrow0$ to obtain $q\le\phi$. Therefore the exact, unregularized envelope equality is
$$P_L(f)=p_0^*P_{L_0}(f_0).                                             \tag{10.2}$$
It is continuous and genuine. The proof bound every arbitrary competitor through finite feasible majorants; it did not suppose an arbitrary psh net had a common countable field of definition.

PL density and the elementary inequality $\|P(f)-P(g)\|_\infty\le\|f-g\|_\infty$ extend continuity and genuine membership to every finite continuous obstacle: approximate uniformly by rational PL, and use uniform closure of PSH. BJ 5.17 gives EP for the rational ample class. For every real ample numerical class $\alpha$, choose rational ample $\omega_j\to\alpha$ with $\omega_j-\alpha$ ample, hence nef. Such a sequence exists in the finite-dimensional numerical space by openness of the ample cone and a small positive displacement toward a fixed rational ample direction. Constants are psh in each nef difference, so $\operatorname{PSH}(\alpha)\subset\operatorname{PSH}(\omega_j)$ by BJ 4.7. For any bounded-above family of $\alpha$-psh functions, its usc supremum is $\omega_j$-psh by EP there. BJ varying-class closure makes it $\alpha$-psh. This proves EP for all ample numerical classes over arbitrary-cardinality $k$, conditional on countable EP, with no missing operator premise in the continuous transfer (9.1).

## 11. Normalization is onto only after target EP

The finite birational universal homeomorphism $\nu:X^\nu\to X$ induces a homeomorphism on analytifications: each finite radicial fiber has just one analytic point, since its unique residue-field norm is fixed, and a proper continuous bijection of compact Hausdorff spaces is a homeomorphism. This is a topological assertion and does not alone give genuine psh descent.

There is an explicit conductor blowup realizing $\nu$. Write $B=\nu_*\mathcal O_{X^\nu}$ and $J=\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_X}(B/\mathcal O_X)$. It is a nonzero coherent ideal: clearing the denominators of finitely many integral generators of the finite birational algebra produces a nonzero conductor element. Choose an ample $A$ and a nonzero section $a\in H^0(X,J\otimes A)$ after sufficiently large twisting. In a frame of $A$ let $a_U$ be its coefficient and put $I|_U=a_UB|_U\subset\mathcal O_U$. These ideals agree on overlaps because the frame ratios are units of $\mathcal O_X$, hence of $B$. They form a coherent nonzero ideal of $\mathcal O_X$.

On an affine integral chart $A_0\subset B_0$, $I=aB_0$ and $I^m=a^mB_0$ for $m\ge1$. Its Rees algebra is $A_0\oplus\bigoplus_{m\ge1}a^mB_0t^m$. The single chart $D_+(at)$ covers its Proj. To see this, every degree-one generator $abt$ with $b$ integral over $A_0$ has a monic equation whose coefficients in degree $j$ contain $(at)^j$; a homogeneous prime containing $at$ consequently contains all degree-one generators, hence the irrelevant ideal, and is not a Proj point. In the localization the degree-zero ring is exactly $B_0$, since $(abt)/(at)=b$ and all degree-zero fractions are in $B_0$. Thus $\operatorname{Bl}_I(X)=X^\nu$ scheme-theoretically, and these chart identities glue. This calculation does not use a conductor ideal with incorrectly asserted invertible pullback.

Now, **after** Section 10 proves target EP conditionally for every ample numerical class, choose target $\theta_m=(1+m^{-1})c_1(L)>c_1(L)$. BJ 5.13 applies and gives the genuine homeomorphism
$$\nu^*:\operatorname{PSH}(X,L)\xrightarrow{\sim}
\operatorname{PSH}(X^\nu,\nu^*L).                                      \tag{11.1}$$
The conductor calculation also justifies its blowup presentation in the lemma's proof. This application is not used to obtain the first target EP. Actual suprema agree by surjectivity, and continuous functions correspond because $\nu^{\rm an}$ is a homeomorphism.

## 12. Exact mixed products, energy, and finite-energy transport

The general-variety scope of BJ is essential. Its initial conventions allow reduced nonnormal varieties, and Section 7 resumes that scope. The genuine pairing and operator already exist there, independently of EP. Let $V=(L^n)>0$ and use the raw operator
$$\mathrm{MA}^{\rm raw}_L(\psi)=(c_1(L)+dd^c\psi)^n,
\qquad \mathrm{MA}_L=V^{-1}\mathrm{MA}^{\rm raw}_L.                        \tag{12.1}$$
The normalization is a calibration, not a definition of a different inverse measure.

BJ Proposition 7.2, equation (7.5), gives equality of the genuine mixed energy pairings under normalization pullback; Proposition 7.19, equation (7.18), gives
$$\nu_*\bigwedge_j(c_1(\nu^*L_j)+dd^c\nu^*\psi_j)
=\bigwedge_j(c_1(L_j)+dd^c\psi_j)                                      \tag{12.2}$$
for genuine signed finite-energy entries in its stated scope. This already includes unbounded entries; it is not inferred by taking an arbitrary formal weak limit. At the model level normalization has degree one, sends its fundamental cycle to $[X]$, and is an isomorphism at generic vertical DVRs, so $b_E$ and the projected intersection coefficients agree. For general entries the source extends the actual symmetric pairing using monotone energy continuity and defines the signed Radon measure by testing rational PL; density identifies the measure. Both normalizations in (12.1) use the same $V$, by the degree-one projection formula.

Put
$$E_L(\psi)=\frac{\langle(c_1(L),\psi)^{n+1}\rangle}{(n+1)V},\qquad
\mathcal E^1(X,L)=\{\psi\in\operatorname{PSH}(X,L):E_L(\psi)>-\infty\}.
$$
For arbitrary genuine psh inputs the energy is the decreasing extension of the bounded energy. Floors pull back exactly, and their raw pairings are equal by 7.2. Monotone continuity therefore gives
$$E_L(\psi)=E_{\nu^*L}(\nu^*\psi),                                      \tag{12.3}$$
including the value $-\infty$. Once (11.1) is known, this proves onto $\mathcal E^1$ and its weak and strong topological compatibility: the weak topologies use the identical divisorial valuations, and the strong ones add continuity of this same energy. There is no use of I-Cauchy completion to manufacture an operator or a potential.

The target measure is a positive Radon measure $\eta$ with **raw mass $V$**, satisfying
$$E_L^\vee(\eta/V)=\sup_{\psi\in\mathcal E^1(X,L)}
\left(E_L(\psi)-\int\psi\,d(\eta/V)\right)<\infty.                       \tag{12.4}$$
BJ 9.20 on irreducible general $X$ equates this with integrability of every genuine $\mathcal E^1$ potential. No skeleton or support restriction appears. Transport $\eta$ through the analytic normalization homeomorphism to $\eta^\nu$. Equations (11.1)--(12.3) and the ordinary change-of-variables formula give equal dual energies, equivalent integrability conditions and exact mass. Formula (12.2) then transports actual finite-energy solutions and all mixed products. Nilpotent cycle factors from a model or a different field are retained throughout; the only topological reductions were in Section 6.

## 13. Conditional variational equation, with all replacements

Conditional on EP obtained above, the actual general-variety theorem is BJ **12.8**, whose equivalence includes onto finite-energy MA. We record the proof ingredients rather than substituting the smooth corollary 12.9.

* Compactness is target normalized compactness, equivalent to EP by BJ 5.11. On countable targets it was transferred from smooth **nef** compactness only under C1-original. On arbitrary-cardinality targets Section 10 proves EP by finite obstacle and finite competitor descent. No metrizable compactness or countable net was silently assumed.
* Envelopes are genuine on the original variety and original ample bundle by (10.2), PL density, varying-class closure and BJ 5.17. Orthogonality uses the nonnegative integral (10.1). The new Wu v1 envelope proof is not an independent proof of this gate: its LF2697--2755 explicitly invokes resolved-nef descent and its weak/global theorem.
* Energy differentiation is BJ 8.5--8.6 for the **outer** decreasing energy $E^\downarrow$, on the reduced-projective general scope. For PL $g$ it gives $E^\downarrow(\psi+tg)=E(\psi)+t\int g\,\mathrm{MA}_L(\psi)+O(t^2)$; uniform PL density and the Lipschitz bound give the continuous-test derivative. Under EP, $E^\downarrow(\psi+tg)=E_L(P_L(\psi+tg))$. The derivative concerns genuine energy and the genuine operator, not an auxiliary law.
* Actual attainment uses a normalized maximizing sequence for (12.4). It has $J_{\eta/V}\to0$. BJ's bound (9.11) makes $J$ eventually bounded.
